title: Loop language: clauses from ASP
description: The check derives the refinement itself: clause(Id, Atom, Value) means "Atom must have Value"; the atoms with one Id form one clause (one of them must hold).

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% Rules every solver needs. The constant n is set in the Loop tab.
num(1..n).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% Solver A proposes candidates: here, any set of numbers.
{ pick(X) : num(X) }.
#show pick/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The atoms solver A and solver C share. glue(T) makes T an interface atom:
% its value in a candidate is fixed when the check runs.
glue(pick(X)) :- num(X).
fragments.description: The interface atoms: every glue(T) makes T an interface atom.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% Solver C looks for a counterexample: a sum X + Y = Z inside the candidate.
1 { sum(X,Y) : num(X), num(Y), X <= Y, X + Y <= n } 1.
:- sum(X,Y), not pick(X).
:- sum(X,Y), not pick(Y).
:- sum(X,Y), not pick(X+Y).
#show sum/2.

% One clause: one of the three numbers must leave the set.
clause(1, pick(X), false) :- sum(X,Y).
clause(1, pick(Y), false) :- sum(X,Y).
clause(1, pick(X+Y), false) :- sum(X,Y).
fragments.description: Looks for a counterexample to a candidate (solver C) and marks the atoms it depends on with relevant/1.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# G.clauses(X) reads the refinement from the counterexample itself: the check
# fragment derives clause(Id, Atom, Value) atoms, one clause per Id.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X: reject M with G.clauses(X)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The same refinement in a Shape 2 loop: A is solved again after each clause.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clauses(X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))
